Hi Yannick,

I have an update for you. I created a test copy of the Internal Theft Report-2025 Employee Information report using Save As — without changing any fields or settings — and the copy is working correctly. All incident data, employee details, and amounts are populating as expected, and the CTE syntax error is gone.

What this tells us is that the original report definitions are carrying stale query data from before the migration. When Izenda rebuilds the report through Save As, it generates fresh SQL against the current database and everything resolves correctly.

Could you try this with a couple of your other reports that are showing the same error? Just open the report, do a Save As with a new name, and check if the copy works. If that clears it up across the board, you should be able to replace your originals without needing to wait on a code fix.

Let me know how it goes and we can go from there.

Thank you,
Tyrone Whitney

Option 1 — Client Self-Service (Save As)
Yannick opens each broken report, does Save As with a new name, no changes needed. The copy generates fresh SQL and works immediately. Only incident-sourced reports need this — audit reports are fine. Fastest path, zero engineering involvement. Downside: manual, report by report.

Option 2 — Solution Expert Assistance (Save As at Scale)
Route to Dan Ortquist (he built these reports originally). He can Save As all affected reports in one session, verify each copy renders correctly, and clean up the old versions. Same fix mechanism as Option 1, but handled by someone who knows the report library and can do it systematically without the client fumbling through it. This is the right path if Yannick pushes back on doing it himself.

Option 3 — Engineering Fix (SQL Server Compatibility Level)
One ALTER DATABASE command to adjust the compatibility level on the Platform Cohesion SQL instance. Fixes the entire class of CTE errors permanently — no report-by-report work needed. But it requires Engineering evaluation, testing across all clients on that instance, and a maintenance window. Not a quick turnaround. This should still happen eventually regardless of which option resolves PVH, because the next migrated client with CTE-based reports will hit the same wall.

One more thing — are you trying to export from the original reports, or from the new copies we created together using Save As? This makes a difference because the Save As copies generate fresh queries against the new database, so they may behave differently than the originals.

Thank you,

Export tested on the PVH tenant on 21 August, HAR captured and attached.

The report itself is healthy. Rows render and the filter dropdowns populate. The SQL syntax error captured on 30 June does not reproduce. Only the export path is still broken.

Three requests, 1.5 seconds:

  1. GET rs.aspx?output=XLS(MIME)&&refrn=Admin+Reports\\0-+Internal+Theft+Report-2025-+Employee+Information&taskId=5d26b176-c81e-1469-4327-5a304ef0f10e
    302, location: /pvh/nettrack/AdHoc/rs.aspx?fid=ba3a7a06-cdb2-4df0-a40a-cdcbaf67eb8e, 1286 ms

  2. POST rs.aspx
    body: wscmd=taskexists&wsarg0=5d26b176-c81e-1469-4327-5a304ef0f10e
    response: {"Value":"false","AdditionalData":["5d26b176-c81e-1469-4327-5a304ef0f10e"]}

  3. GET rs.aspx?fid=ba3a7a06-cdb2-4df0-a40a-cdcbaf67eb8e
    200, content-type text/html, content-length 0, no content-disposition header

The server issues a file id and then reports that the export task does not exist. The client polls taskexists on the taskId it sent and gets false back. The follow up request returns an empty html body, so there is no file and no download instruction for the browser.

The client polls 5d26b176 while the server redirects to ba3a7a06. Different identifiers.

Linked to ENG-5649. Its description no longer matches this tenant, see the comment posted there.
